contradictions.fact: Waypoint list names 'Red Pass' as a mid-route junction, but the route's own prose never goes there

claims.says: {"name":"Red Pass","type":"Junction","lat":47.4592466,"lng":-121.3954014}

...turn left (west) onto Trail #1033, the Commonwealth Creek Trail...As the trail levels out near a small tarn/pond below Red Mountain's west slope, watch for a cairn planted in the middle of the path — this marks the scramble takeoff point...
Leave PCT North Trailhead -> Commonwealth Creek Trail (#1033) junction -> Reach the pond below the west face -> Ascend boot path to summit (no Red Pass stop listed)
...to Red Mountain Saddle/Red Pass (approx. 5,320+ ft), passing the Red Mountain scramble boot path along the way

contradictions.why: The Standard Scramble's own beta/approach/itinerary describe leaving the trail at a cairn near an unnamed tarn (~4,600 ft) and never mention Red Pass, yet the route's waypoint list places 'Red Pass' as a junction between the trailhead and the summit. The area's other route (East Ridge) independently describes Red Pass (~5,320+ ft) as a further, higher point along the same trail that this route's cairn turnoff is reached before — so Red Pass does not sit on this route's line as described.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The approach/beta/itinerary (3 fields) agree on a cairn/tarn turnoff with no mention of Red Pass; the waypoint entry looks contaminated from a neighboring route's data.

contradictions.fact: dist_km is one-way while the itinerary/total note give round-trip mileage

claims.says: A single long day: ~8 miles round trip, 2,900 ft gain...

contradictions.why: 6.45 km (~4.0 mi) is almost exactly half of the itinerary's 8-mile round-trip figure, so dist_km reads as one-way while the header/itinerary distance is round-trip — the page could show two different 'distance' numbers for the same day.
contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary.miles (8) and totalNote agree with each other and with approach_variants distMi=8; dist_km is the one-way convention noted elsewhere in this codebase as inconsistent.

contradictions.fact: Route's own approach names a saddle belonging to a different peak (Lundin/East Lundin) rather than Red Mountain

claims.says: The route begins at the saddle between Lundin and East Lundin peaks; follow a climber's path west/up to the base of the route.
Confirm which summit (Red Mountain vs. neighboring Lundin Peak) you intend to top out on before committing — see route notes.

the published location text for this route refers to a saddle between Lundin and East Lundin peaks, while the approach it gives goes to Red Pass and then west, which is Red Mountain's ground rather than Lundin's...Three descriptions, one name.
5890 (matches Red Mountain's own summit elevation, not a Lundin-area point)

contradictions.why: The route's own 'approach' field names a saddle associated with a neighboring peak (Lundin/East Lundin), not Red Mountain, while the rest of the route's data (area filing, high_point_ft, watch_out) treats it as a Red Mountain route — and the route's own baseFinding text explicitly flags this as a real naming confusion 'that could send you to another mountain.'
contradictions.internal_resolution: baseFinding says to identify the route by 'the saddle and the three bolts, not by the route name,' treating the Red Pass approach (Red Mountain) as correct and the Lundin/East Lundin saddle wording as the error — but this is stated nowhere in the primary 'approach' field itself.

contradictions.fact: Stated season excludes October, but seasonal guidance includes it

claims.says: Jul-Sep
August is peak-optimal; the broader viable window runs mid-July through October data
{"status":"marginal","reason":"Shorter daylight and increasing chance of early snow/ice on the steep loose path toward the tail end of the season window"}

contradictions.why: October falls entirely outside the route's stated Jul-Sep season (shown in the header/Trip-plan season chip), yet the route's own seasonal_guidance names October as part of the 'broader viable window' and gives it a status — the guidance window is wider than the season, not a best-window-inside-a-season case.

contradictions.fact: Pitch count (5) exceeds the numbered rows in pitch_detail (4)

claims.says: 4 numbered pitch rows (1, 2, 3, 4)
climb 4-6 pitches of ice/mixed/snow

contradictions.why: The header/TECHNICAL STATS would show 5 pitches, but the ROUTE BREAKDOWN table (pitch_detail) only lists 4 numbered pitches — a climber counting pitches from the breakdown gets a different number than the stat.

contradictions.fact: Overview's stated route length (~1,300 ft) is roughly double length_m and the pitch-length total

claims.says: it's a roughly 1,300-ft alpine route following a prominent gully system to a distinctive 'box gully' feature...

contradictions.why: The overview describes the route as about 1,300 vertical feet, while the TECHNICAL STATS climb-length field (length_m=213m≈699ft) and the sum of the four listed pitch lengths (≈607ft) both land at roughly half that figure.

contradictions.fact: Whether walking off via Pineapple Pass/South Face is a valid alternative to rappelling

claims.says: Rappel the route (P6 down to P1) rather than descending via Pineapple Pass, using the bolted anchors.
...alternatively walk off via the South Face descent.
Some parties instead walk off toward Pineapple Pass and descend the South Face's scramble descent.
...rappel the route or walk off -> retrace the approach to the trailhead.

contradictions.why: The short 'descent' field states the route is rappelled 'rather than' walking off via Pineapple Pass, while rappels, descent_text, and the itinerary string all present walking off as a legitimate alternative descent option.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Three fields (rappels, descent_text, itinerary) agree walk-off is a real option; the single 'descent' field is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Gear implies a roped/belayed summit pitch, but the route is described elsewhere as an unroped scramble to the true summit

claims.says: Small cams (0.4-0.5 C4 size) or nuts — the top pitch's belay isn't bolted, so you need gear to build the summit anchor
Unroped scrambling to the true summit; single bolt en route but no anchor at the top.
...seven-pitch (six roped pitches plus a short summit scramble)...
the anchor is unequipped at the true summit — P7 is an unroped scramble with no rappel anchor

contradictions.why: The gear list implies the party belays a final pitch and needs cams/nuts to build a 'summit anchor,' while the overview, the pitch table, and descent_text all agree the stretch to the true summit is unroped scrambling with no anchor at all.

contradictions.fact: rappels field calls the 4 standard rappel stations 'bolted,' but the per-station detail describes natural (tree/horn/block) anchors

claims.says: 4 rappels (roughly 25-30m / under 100ft each) from bolted/slung anchors back down to Pineapple Pass
3 rap rings, backed by sling around tree/horn
two slung trees
several slings + 3 rap rings around a block
A separate, partly hidden bolted line beside pitches 1 and 2 exists so that ascending and descending parties are not in the same place; it is a different set of anchors, not a variation.

contradictions.why: The summary 'rappels' field calls the standard descent's anchors 'bolted,' but every one of the 4 detailed stations is a tree, horn, or block sling (with rap rings/cordelette added, not drilled bolts), and the route's own note says bolted anchors belong to a separate line beside pitches 1-2, not these 4 stations.
contradictions.internal_resolution: rappel_detail (4 stations) and rappel_count_note agree the standard line is natural/slung anchors; the 'bolted' word in the summary rappels field appears to be the error.

contradictions.fact: gain_ft/loss_ft (2,500) disagree with the itinerary day's gainFt/lossFt (3,000)

claims.says: ...about 6.5 miles and 3,000 ft of gain over 5-6 pitches...

contradictions.why: The route-level gain_ft/loss_ft and approach_variants agree on 2,500 ft, but the itinerary day and its own totalNote both state 3,000 ft for the same car-to-car climb — a 20% gap between the header/TECHNICAL STATS number and the Trip-plan TOTAL row.
contradictions.internal_resolution: gain_ft, loss_ft, and approach_variants (3 fields) agree at 2,500 ft; the itinerary/totalNote pair is the outlier at 3,000 ft.

contradictions.fact: descent_text describes 2 rappels down the NE side to Pineapple Pass, but rappel_detail describes joining the South Face's 4-rappel line at the summit

claims.says: From the summit, downclimb a short distance to a tree anchor just below/west of the true summit. From there, two rappels — up to 60m each...drop down the NE side to the notch (Pineapple Pass)...From the notch you join the South Face (standard) descent...
First rappel of the standard South Face descent that Northeast Slabs climbers join at the summit.

Standard descent follows the South Face rappel line (4 raps, roughly 25-30m each) back to Pineapple Pass; some winter parties instead make 2 long rappels (60m) from a tree below the summit directly down to the notch before skiing out.

contradictions.why: descent_text's main narrative has the party rappel twice down the NE side to reach Pineapple Pass before joining the South Face descent, while the route's own detailed rappel_detail table (identical station-by-station text to the South Face route) instead has climbers join the South Face's 4-rappel sequence immediately at the summit — two different physical descent lines both presented as what happens.

contradictions.fact: climate.winter and climate.spring each give a different season end-point than season/best_season

claims.says: Dec-Apr (winter-spring; condition-dependent), first climbed in winter
Winter-spring (roughly December-April) once enough snow and ice have built up...
Primary season (Dec-Mar) for the route as a mixed/ice line...
Consolidating snowpack can offer workable mixed/snow conditions March-May, but the crux corner's ice/snow coverage is highly variable

contradictions.why: season and best_season both give December through April, but climate.winter narrows the 'primary season' to Dec-Mar (dropping April) while climate.spring separately extends workable conditions out to May (beyond the stated season) — three different end months for when the route stops being climbable.
